message.content:
Below are two ways to create a **Google Cloud Compute Engine** instance that has an **NVIDIA RTX A6000 GPU** and runs **Ubuntu 20.04 LTS**:

| Method | What you’ll run | Where it lives |
|--------|-----------------|----------------|
| **gcloud CLI** | `gcloud compute instances create …` | Your terminal (requires the Cloud SDK) |
| **REST API** | `POST https://compute.googleapis.com/...` | Any HTTP client (curl, Postman, your own code) |

> **NOTE**  
> *Google Cloud does not use the term “EC2”; that’s Amazon Web Services. In GCP the equivalent is a Compute Engine instance.*  
> *Make sure you have the Compute Engine API enabled, a project with GPU quota, and a service account with the right scopes.*

---

## 1. gcloud CLI

```bash
# Variables – change these to match your environment
PROJECT="my-gcp-project"
ZONE="us-central1-a"
INSTANCE_NAME="rtx-a6000-ubuntu"
MACHINE_TYPE="n1-standard-8"          # 8 vCPU, 30 GB RAM
GPU_COUNT=1
GPU_TYPE="nvidia-tesla-a6000"
DISK_SIZE_GB=100
DISK_TYPE="pd-ssd"
IMAGE_FAMILY="ubuntu-2004-lts"
IMAGE_PROJECT="ubuntu-os-cloud"

# Create the instance
gcloud compute instances create "$INSTANCE_NAME" \
  --project="$PROJECT" \
  --zone="$ZONE" \
  --machine-type="$MACHINE_TYPE" \
  --accelerator="type=$GPU_TYPE,count=$GPU_COUNT" \
  --boot-disk-size="$DISK_SIZE_GB" \
  --boot-disk-type="$DISK_TYPE" \
  --image-family="$IMAGE_FAMILY" \
  --image-project="$IMAGE_PROJECT" \
  --maintenance-policy=MIGRATE \
  --scopes=https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform \
  --metadata-from-file startup-script=startup.sh   # optional
```

### What each flag does

| Flag | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `--machine-type` | CPU/RAM configuration |
| `--accelerator` | Attach GPU(s) – type and count |
| `--boot-disk-size` / `--boot-disk-type` | Disk size & performance |
| `--image-family` / `--image-project` | Ubuntu 20.04 LTS image |
| `--maintenance-policy=MIGRATE` | Keeps the GPU attached during maintenance |
| `--scopes` | Gives the instance full Cloud Platform access (needed for GPU drivers) |
| `--metadata-from-file startup-script` | Optional script that runs on first boot (e.g., install NVIDIA drivers) |

> **Tip:** If you want to automatically install the NVIDIA driver on boot, create a `startup.sh` file with the official NVIDIA driver install script and reference it as shown above.

---

## 2. REST API (curl)

```bash
# Variables – change these to match your environment
PROJECT="my-gcp-project"
ZONE="us-central1-a"
INSTANCE_NAME="rtx-a6000-ubuntu"
ACCESS_TOKEN="ya29.a0AfH6SM..."   # OAuth 2.0 token with Compute scope

# JSON body – the instance definition
read -r -d '' INSTANCE_JSON <<EOF
{
  "name": "$INSTANCE_NAME",
  "machineType": "zones/$ZONE/machineTypes/n1-standard-8",
  "disks": [
    {
      "boot": true,
      "autoDelete": true,
      "initializeParams": {
        "sourceImage": "projects/ubuntu-os-cloud/global/images/family/ubuntu-2004-lts",
        "diskSizeGb": 100,
        "diskType": "projects/$PROJECT/zones/$ZONE/diskTypes/pd-ssd"
      }
    }
  ],
  "networkInterfaces": [
    {
      "network": "global/networks/default",
      "accessConfigs": [
        { "type": "ONE_TO_ONE_NAT", "name": "External NAT" }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "accelerators": [
    {
      "acceleratorType": "projects/$PROJECT/zones/$ZONE/acceleratorTypes/nvidia-tesla-a6000",
      "acceleratorCount": 1
    }
  ],
  "serviceAccounts": [
    {
      "email": "default",
      "scopes": ["https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform"]
    }
  ],
  "metadata": {
    "items": [
      {
        "key": "startup-script",
        "value": "#!/bin/bash\nsudo apt-get update\nsudo apt-get install -y nvidia-driver-535"
      }
    ]
  }
}
EOF

# POST request
curl -X POST \
  "https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/$PROJECT/zones/$ZONE/instances" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ACCESS_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d "$INSTANCE_JSON"
```

### How to get the `ACCESS_TOKEN`

```bash
gcloud auth application-default print-access-token
```

or use a service account key:

```bash
gcloud auth activate-service-account --key-file=service-account.json
gcloud auth print-access-token
```

---

## Quick Checklist

| ✅ | Item |
|----|------|
| 1 | **Compute Engine API** enabled in your project. |
| 2 | **GPU quota** for `nvidia-tesla-a6000` in the chosen zone. |
| 3 | **Service account** with `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform` scope. |
| 4 | **Firewall** rules allowing SSH (port 22) if you want to connect. |
| 5 | **Optional**: `startup-script` to install NVIDIA drivers automatically. |

Once the instance is running, you can SSH into it:

```bash
gcloud compute ssh "$INSTANCE_NAME" --zone="$ZONE"
```

And verify the GPU:

```bash
nvidia-smi
```

That’s it! You now have a Compute Engine instance with an RTX A6000 GPU running Ubuntu 20.04 LTS.
